title: BlitzScale: Fast and Live Large Model Autoscaling with O(1) Host Caching
problem: Model autoscaling faces a fundamental trade-off between scaling speed and storage/memory usage for parameter caching. The data plane is slow and blocking—scaled instances halt while parameters load—preventing frequent multi-host scaling.
motivation: Model autoscaling is critical for serverless model-as-a-service platforms to dynamically handle varying workloads and serve large language models efficiently.
method: BlitzScale sends model parameters through the direct network between GPUs, which is typically underutilized, instead of slower storage paths. It maintains a constant-sized cache on each host that doesn't grow as models get larger, providing efficient memory usage. Rather than scaling entire computing instances at once (which must pause while parameters load), it scales individual model layers, allowing computational work to start on newly added GPUs before parameters fully finish loading. The system uses network broadcast sending (multicast) to efficiently deliver parameters to multiple instances without excessive caching overhead.
key_novelty: BlitzScale eliminates autoscaling delays by loading parameters through the GPU-to-GPU network with a constant-sized cache, and scaling individual layers so computing instances never block waiting for parameters to arrive.
contributions: Fast data plane for loading model checkpoints via inter-GPU compute network with minimal host caching
Live autoscaling via layer-level scaling abstraction that offloads computation before parameters fully load
Network-optimized multicast approach for efficient multi-instance scaling
BlitzLoad: lightweight checkpoint engine for integration with vLLM and SGLang with minimal code changes

metrics.speedup: 94% lower tail latency vs ServerlessLLM; 49% lower serving GPU time vs DistServe and vLLM
metrics.other: Achieves improvements while maintaining same SLA

primary_theme: GPU cluster autoscaling for LLM inference
